property.name: yarn.resourcemanager.hostname
property.description: Master's mesh IP. Setting this one property derives the scheduler, resource-tracker, admin and web-app addresses automatically.

property.name: yarn.nodemanager.aux-services
property.description: Without this the reduce phase cannot fetch map output and the job hangs at "reduce 0%". Required on EVERY NodeManager - a node that is missing it will run maps and then stall the whole job.

property.name: yarn.nodemanager.hostname
property.description: CHANGE PER NODE. The address this NodeManager advertises to the ResourceManager. Must be resolvable from the master.

property.name: yarn.nodemanager.resource.memory-mb
property.description: RAM this node offers to containers. Deliberately modest: these are laptops that also run a desktop, a browser and WSL2's own overhead. Five nodes x 2048 MB = 10240 MB of cluster memory.

property.name: yarn.nodemanager.resource.cpu-vcores
property.description: Two vcores per node, ten across the cluster.

property.name: yarn.scheduler.maximum-allocation-mb
property.description: Ceiling for a single container request. Must be at or below the per-node memory above, otherwise the scheduler accepts a request that no node can ever satisfy and the application waits forever.

property.name: yarn.nodemanager.vmem-check-enabled
property.description: The virtual-memory check compares a JVM's reserved address space against a multiple of its physical allocation. Under WSL2 that reservation is large and the check kills healthy containers. The physical-memory check below is the one that actually protects the host, and it stays on.
